properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 by breaking CI with it. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT HAPPENED, and it is the cleanest possible demonstration. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` shipped, and the first thing it was pointed at was the document that actually drove reflow2's governance work: `dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, in a SIBLING REPOSITORY. Registered as `art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback` with `location: ../dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, plus DOCUMENTS edges to the seven governance requirements. Local gates passed. CI FAILED:

  FAIL  DRIFT  art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback: missing_artifact

CI checks out reflow2 alone, so the path resolves to nothing. `tools/reflow2_check.py` (line 615) reads `location` and FALLS BACK TO `name` when it is absent, then joins against `--root` — so there is NO WAY to register an out-of-repo source without failing the gate. Dropping the location does not help; it makes the check try the name as a path instead.

⭐ THIS IS `req:content-reaches-every-seat` FIRING ON THE THING BUILT TO SATISFY `req:no-idea-goes-quiet`. "A pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the machine that wrote it." A relative path into a sibling checkout resolves on exactly one machine. The two accepted requirements pull against each other in this case, and neither names the other.

⚠️ THE CASE IS NOT EXOTIC — IT IS ANTHONY'S NORMAL. His operating context is several partially-built designs across repositories and organizations, with the source material for one living in another. `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` (proposed) is the axis; this is a concrete instance of it landing on the artifact layer rather than the design layer.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) An `external: true` / `reachability` marker on Artifact that tells `reconcile_artifacts` the file is deliberately not part of this checkout, so ABSENCE is expected rather than drift. Mirrors what `volatility` already does for expected CONTENT change — this is the same move for expected ABSENCE. Risk: absence is the one finding `set_artifact_intent` deliberately keeps at full severity, so this weakens the strongest signal in the reconcile family and needs its own argument.
(b) COPY the driving excerpt into this repo as a dated, attributed source document and register that. Honest, resolves everywhere, and is what `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed` (accepted) arguably already implies — keep the source WITH the design. Cost: a copy can drift from its original, and nothing would detect that.
(c) Treat the other repo as a DESIGN rather than a folder, and reach it through the cross-design machinery (`req:design-dependencies-declared`, accepted) instead of the artifact layer. Cleanest conceptually; costs the most, and dev_storyflow's feedback file is not a design.
(d) Do nothing, and accept that a source outside the repo simply cannot be traced. Cheapest; it is also the status quo that made Anthony hand-point an agent at the file in the first place.

WHAT WAS DONE MEANWHILE: the artifact and its seven DOCUMENTS edges were REMOVED so the gate is honest, and the backward trace is once again absent. That is a retreat, not a fix, and it is recorded here so the retreat is visible rather than quiet. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` remains correct for the in-repo case, which is the case its own description scoped it to — it says nothing about reachability, and that silence is the actual defect in it.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a design register a source document that lives OUTSIDE its own repository?
properties.rationale: The capability shipped and its first real use broke CI, because the only source document that mattered lives in a sibling repo. Two accepted requirements — no-idea-goes-quiet and content-reaches-every-seat — pull in opposite directions here and neither names the other. Recording the fork rather than picking one, because option (a) weakens the strongest signal the reconcile family has and option (b) crosses a repo boundary; both are Anthony's calls.
